question: After emergency surgery for a perforated peptic ulcer (closure with an omental patch), testing for and eradicating Helicobacter pylori is mandatory to prevent ulcer recurrence.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. H. pylori eradication is essential after perforated peptic ulcer repair — without it, the ulcer will very likely recur. Testing (CLO test / serology / UBT) and treatment should be arranged before or after discharge.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. H. pylori is present in ~70-80% of duodenal ulcer perforations. After repair, failure to test and eradicate H. pylori results in a high recurrence rate. Triple therapy (PPI + two antibiotics) is standard post-operative management.
